test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If 3x + 2y = 10 and 2xy = 7, then find the value of 3x - 2y (if 3x - 2y > 0).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct identity relation between sum and difference:

(3x − 2y)² = (3x + 2y)² − 4 × (3x) × (2y)

⇒ (3x − 2y)² = (10)² − 12 × (2xy)

⇒ (3x − 2y)² = 100 − 12 × 7 = 16

⇒ 3x − 2y = √16 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

3x + 2y = 10

2xy = 7

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 3x and b = 2y

⇒ Product 4ab = 4 × (3x) × (2y) = 24xy

⇒ Apply the formula: (3x − 2y)² = (3x + 2y)² − 24xy

⇒ Substitute the value 2xy = 7 into the expression for 24xy:

⇒ 24xy = 12 × 2xy = 12 × 7 = 84

⇒ Substitute the sum and the product into the main identity:

⇒ (3x − 2y)² = (10)² − 84

⇒ (3x − 2y)² = 100 − 84

⇒ (3x − 2y)² = 16

⇒ Taking the square root on both sides:

⇒ 3x − 2y = ±√16

⇒ 3x − 2y = 4 (Since it is given that 3x − 2y > 0)

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square of a Sum

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

Square of a Difference

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

Sum and Difference Relation

(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab. This identity helps to easily convert the sum of two numbers into their difference and vice versa when the product is known.
